question: Assume today is 2026-08-29. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of people who moved between municipalities within Japan in August 2026 (Japanese and foreign residents combined), as first reported in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration.

target.what: Number of internal migration events (moves between municipalities) within Japan recorded in the Basic Resident Registration system and first published in the Statistics Bureau of Japan's monthly Report on Internal Migration in Japan Derived from the Basic Resident Registration, for moves occurring i
target.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications)
target.cadence: monthly, with preliminary figures for the reference month typically released about 1-2 months after month-end (e.g., August data around late September/October)
target.caveats: The August 2026 report would normally be published after the 2026-08-29 cutoff, so the target period is completed but the official figure is not yet published at cutoff; the estimate must be built from prior-year August values, year-to-date 2026 partial data, and seasonal/structural adjustments. candidates.hypothesis: August internal migration in Japan follows a stable seasonal pattern (August is typically a high-migration month due to summer job/relocation season and student moves). Prior-year August totals and the 2026 monthly year-to-date series (Jan-Jul 2026) anchor the level and trend; August 2026 ≈ August 2025 × (2026 YTD growth factor) × seasonal factor.

Minimum: August 2025 total and Jan-Jul 2026 monthly totals.

The repair keeps the round-1 route's structure (August level scaled by the July 2025-to-July 2026 YoY change) but the code cannot execute it without an August 2025 target. Since no kept point gives August 2025, this method is dropped and replaced by m4, which uses the same July YoY signal applied to an August 2025 level built from p174 and the a4 August/July ratio. This preserves the round-1 yoy_scaling idea (last year's August scaled by the July YoY change) using only kept points. It shares p174 and a1 with m2/m3, so it is not an independent route; the main failure mode is the assumed August/July ratio.

assumptions.name: August 2026 vs August 2025 YoY change factor for all inter-municipal movers
assumptions.rationale: July 2026 was -1.9% YoY (p27 vs p174) with Japanese movers -2.7% (p32 vs p177) and foreign movers +3.2% (p34 vs p180); January 2026 showed the same pattern (p314 vs p318, p315 vs p317). A modest continued decline near -2% is the central value; the range allows for foreign-mover acceleration or a Japanese-mover rebound.
assumptions.applies_when: The July 2026 YoY trend carries into August 2026 without a large calendar or policy break.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published August 2026 figure outside the range, or evidence of a registration-rule change or Obon-timing shift that moves August 2026 materially away from the July trend.

assumptions.name: August share of the annual inter-municipal migration total
assumptions.rationale: No kept point gives a measured August share of the annual total. August 2023 (p40 = 379,493) is about 7.2% of the 2023 annual total (p3 = 5,263,249), and July 2025 (p174 = 398,417) is about 7.7% of the 2025 annual total (p1 = 5,190,548); August is typically slightly above July because of late-summer relocations, so a share near 8.3% with a range spanning the observed July/August ratios is reasonable.
assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years and August is not an outlier month.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published monthly series showing August shares consistently outside 7.5-9.2% of the annual total.

assumptions.name: Two-year bridge factor from August 2023 to August 2026
assumptions.rationale: The annual total fell from 5,263,249 in 2023 (p3) to 5,190,548 in 2025 (p1), a factor of about 0.986 over two years; the July 2026 YoY trend (p27 vs p174) adds a further small decline. A factor near 0.965 with a wide range reflects the uncertainty in extrapolating a single August observation three years forward.
assumptions.applies_when: The August seasonal pattern and the national migration trend are stable between 2023 and 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 differs sharply from the 2023-2025 trend, for example a large policy or demographic shock.

assumptions.name: August 2025 vs July 2025 level ratio for all inter-municipal movers
assumptions.rationale: Repairs m1: yoy_scaling needs a target value for August 2025, which no kept point supplies. The only observed August level is August 2023 (p40 = 379,493) and the only observed July 2025 level is p174 = 398,417; the August/July ratio in 2023 was 379,493 / (July 2023 implied by p174 and its -1.6% YoY, ~405,000) ≈ 0.94, while August is usually close to or slightly below July in this series. A ratio near 0.97 with a wide range covers the observed 2023 August/July relationship and the possibility that August 2025 was unusually high or low.
assumptions.applies_when: The August-to-July seasonal ratio in 2025 resembles the 2023 ratio and the recent stable seasonal pattern.
assumptions.falsified_by: A published August 2025 or August 2026 figure showing the August/July ratio far outside 0.90-1.05.

previous_assumptions.rationale: July 2026 was -1.9% YoY (p27 vs p174) with Japanese movers -2.7% (p32 vs p177) and foreign movers +3.2% (p34 vs p180); January 2026 showed the same pattern (p314 vs p318, p315 vs p317). previous_assumptions.applies_when: The July 2026 YoY trend carries into August 2026 without a large calendar or policy break.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A published August 2026 figure outside the range, or evidence of a registration-rule change or Obon-timing shift that moves August 2026 materially away from the July trend.

previous_assumptions.name: August share of the annual inter-municipal migration total
previous_assumptions.rationale: No kept point gives a measured August share of the annual total. previous_assumptions.applies_when: The 2026 seasonal shape resembles recent years and August is not an outlier month.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: A published monthly series showing August shares consistently outside 7.5-9.2% of the annual total.

previous_assumptions.name: Two-year bridge factor from August 2023 to August 2026
previous_assumptions.rationale: The annual total fell from 5,263,249 in 2023 (p3) to 5,190,548 in 2025 (p1), a factor of about 0.986 over two years; the July 2026 YoY trend (p27 vs p174) adds a further small decline. A factor near 0.965 with a wide range reflects the uncertainty in extrapolating a single August observation three years forward.
previous_assumptions.applies_when: The August seasonal pattern and the national migration trend are stable between 2023 and 2026.
previous_assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 differs sharply from the 2023-2025 trend, for example a large policy or demographic shock.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.

The magnitude gate (v2.15d) asks the model once, without retrieval, for a rough estimate; whether the evidence-based estimate is more than 2x above or below it can carry the model's memory of the target into one repair. The rough number itself never enters a computation or a prompt; the estimate before that repair is kept in judge_rounds[-1].magnitude_checks[0]. The gate is off in the own-history ablation.
